newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 150 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 150 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 90 billion bolivar ($185 million) auction of 177-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 21.66 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 30 billion bolivars ($62 million) in 268-day bills with a 22.24 percent coupon, and another 30 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 22.84 percent coupon.
Some 90 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday, and another ten billion on Monday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 90 billion bolivar issue. Then 178-, 269- and 358-day notes carried 22.51, 23.14, and 23.77 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened across the curve to 21.66, 23.70 and 24.04 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
